mcs.annual_nonidentified.spec: series with |MCS|>1 under the annual-aggregation MCS (block=3); same formula as mcs.curated_nonidentified

mcs.curated_default_band_max.spec: maximum non-identified count over the same 50-seed default-configuration band as mcs.curated_default_band_min -- equal to it iff the count is invariant to seed choice at the paper's own tuning

mcs.curated_default_band_max_sq.spec: maximum non-identified count over the same 50-seed default-configuration band as mcs.curated_default_band_min_sq, SQUARED loss

mcs.curated_default_band_min.spec: minimum non-identified count over 50 Monte-Carlo seeds at the paper's own default configuration (block=3, B=2000, alpha=0.10), absolute loss

mcs.curated_default_band_min_sq.spec: minimum non-identified count over 50 Monte-Carlo seeds at the paper's own default configuration (block=3, B=2000, alpha=0.10), SQUARED loss -- the loss-function robustness companion to mcs.curated_default_band_min

mcs.curated_grid_max.spec: maximum non-identified count across the same full curated-panel tuning grid as mcs.curated_grid_min -- equal to it iff the count is exactly invariant across every swept configuration

mcs.curated_grid_min.spec: minimum non-identified count (|MCS_abs|>1) across the FULL curated-panel tuning grid (block in {1,2,3,4,6}, B in {2000,5000}, alpha in {0.05,0.10,0.25}, 10 seeds each -- 5*2*3 = 30 cells, 30*10 = 300 nonid_count() evaluations, and since each one runs the MCS once per curated series, 30*10*12 = 3,600 MCS calls in total)

mcs.monthly_nonidentified_range.spec: min and max curated non-identified count over ALL block lengths swept (1, 2, 3, 6, 12, 24), alpha=0.1; computed over the sweep, not read off its endpoints

mcsarch.curated_exact_match.spec: curated series (all 12, not a subset) on which the hand-rolled range-statistic MCS returns the IDENTICAL surviving model set (not merely the same |MCS|) as arch 8.0.0's independent ModelConfidenceSet implementation, alpha=0.10, block=3, B=2000, on the real per-year absolute-loss panels

mcsarch.curated_exact_match_bootstrap_ma.spec: curated series on which this paper's MCS (raw-mean elimination, moving-block bootstrap) returns the identical surviving set as arch 8.0.0 run with the SAME moving-block bootstrap (arch's default is a stationary bootstrap). A series still differing here differs through the elimination rule (raw vs HLN's e_R) and/or residual implementation differences (independent bootstrap draws, p-value convention); the residual after matching BOTH is mcsarch.curated_exact_match_fully_matched. alpha=0.10, block=3, B=2000, seed=0 on both sides

mcsarch.curated_exact_match_fully_matche.spec: curated series on which this paper's MCS run with HLN's e_R elimination rule (mcs_test.mcs(elimination='e_R')) returns the identical surviving set as arch 8.0.0 with a moving-block bootstrap -- bootstrap scheme AND elimination rule both matched, so this is the pure independent-implementation check

mcsarch.curated_size_match.spec: curated series (all 12) on which the hand-rolled and arch implementations return the same |MCS| cardinality, whether or not the member sets are identical

mcsarch.fredmd_classification_flip.spec: FRED-MD population-sweep series where the two implementations disagree not just on cardinality but on the BINARY identified (|MCS|=1) vs non-identified (|MCS|>1) classification itself -- the honest bound on how much the 56/74 headline could move under a different, equally valid implementation, disclosed alongside the tuning- and significance-level sensitivity already reported

mcsarch.fredmd_exact_match.spec: FRED-MD population-sweep series on which the hand-rolled range-statistic MCS returns the IDENTICAL surviving model set as arch 8.0.0's independent implementation, alpha=0.10, block=3, B=2000

mcsarch.fredmd_exact_match_bootstrap_mat.spec: FRED-MD population-sweep series on which this paper's MCS (raw-mean elimination, moving-block bootstrap) returns the identical surviving set as arch 8.0.0 run with the SAME moving-block bootstrap; a series still differing here differs through the elimination rule (raw vs HLN's e_R) and/or residual implementation differences (independent bootstrap draws, p-value convention) -- the residual after matching BOTH is mcsarch.fredmd_exact_match_fully_matched. alpha=0.10, block=3, B=2000, seed=0

mcsarch.fredmd_exact_match_fully_matched.spec: FRED-MD population-sweep series on which this paper's MCS with HLN's e_R rule returns the identical surviving set as arch 8.0.0 with a moving-block bootstrap -- bootstrap scheme and elimination rule both matched: the pure implementation check

mcsarch.fredmd_nonidentified_eR.spec: FRED-MD series non-identified (|MCS| > 1 at alpha=0.10) when the MCS is run with HLN's e_R elimination rule instead of this paper's raw-mean rule, everything else identical -- the elimination-rule sensitivity of the population headline, disclosed alongside the arch-implementation bound (mcsarch.fredmd_classification_flip). The companion field raw_rule is the same count under the paper's rule, recomputed here

mcsarch.fredmd_size_match.spec: FRED-MD population-sweep series on which the hand-rolled and arch implementations return the same |MCS| cardinality
